data.title: Erythrasma — viva
data.summary: Bacterial infections · 7 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Erythrasma** (Bacterial infections)_

**Q1. Causative organism?**
- Corynebacterium minutissimum (Gram-positive diphtheroid)

**Q2. How does it present?**
- Well-defined reddish-brown, finely scaly, slightly wrinkled patches in groins, axillae, submammary folds; interdigital (4th web space) maceration — commonest form
- Usually asymptomatic or mild itch; generalised form in diabetics

**Q3. Associations?**
- Diabetes mellitus (screen), obesity, hyperhidrosis, warm humid climate, poor hygiene, elderly, immunosuppression; may coexist with tinea/candida

**Q4. Wood's lamp finding?**
- Coral-red fluorescence due to porphyrin (coproporphyrin III) — may be absent if recently washed

**Q5. Differential diagnosis?**
- Tinea cruris (active scaly border, central clearing), intertriginous candidiasis (satellite pustules), inverse psoriasis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, pityriasis versicolor

**Q6. Treatment?**
- Topical erythromycin, clindamycin, fusidic acid or azoles (miconazole, clotrimazole — also cover fungi) for 2 weeks; benzoyl peroxide wash
- Oral erythromycin 250 mg four times daily × 14 days or clarithromycin 1 g single dose for extensive disease

**Q7. Other corynebacterial infections?**
- Pitted keratolysis, trichomycosis axillaris (yellow/red/black concretions on axillary hair — C. tenuis)

## Quick spotter facts
- Brown patch in the groin with coral-red fluorescence on Wood's lamp — erythrasma

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Bacterial infections — erythrasma); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.15. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
